questions.q: If a vector $\vec\alpha$ lies in the plane of $\vec\beta$ and $\vec\gamma$, then :
questions.solution: Three coplanar vectors have scalar triple product $0$: $[\vec\alpha,\vec\beta,\vec\gamma]=0$.

questions.topic: Angle between a line and a plane
questions.q: The angle between the line $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k)+t(2\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)$ and the plane $\vec r\cdot(\hat i+\hat j)+4=0$ is :
Distance from the origin to the plane $3x-6y+2z+7=0$ is :
If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are parallel vectors then $[\vec a,\vec c,\vec b]$ is equal to :
questions.solution: $\vec a\parallel\vec b$ makes $\vec a,\vec c,\vec b$ coplanar, so $[\vec a,\vec c,\vec b]=0$.

questions.q: The angle between the lines $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y+1}{-2}$, $z=2$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{2y+3}{3}=\dfrac{z+5}{2}$ is :
questions.solution: Directions $(3,-2,0)$ and $(1,\tfrac32,2)\propto(2,3,4)$. Dot product $6-6+0=0$, so the angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.q: The volume of the parallelepiped with its edges represented by the vectors $\hat i+\hat j$, $\hat i+2\hat j$, $\hat i+\hat j+\pi\hat k$ is :
The value of $[\hat i,\hat j,\hat k]$ is :
questions.solution: $[\hat i,\hat j,\hat k]=\hat i\cdot(\hat j\times\hat k)=\hat i\cdot\hat i=1$.

questions.q: The value of $[\hat i+\hat j,\ \hat j+\hat k,\ \hat k+\hat i]$ is :
The distance between the parallel planes $x+2y+2z=3$ and $x+2y+2z=9$ is :
Find the volume of the parallelepiped whose edges are $2\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k$, $\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$ and $3\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$.
Find $\lambda$ if $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$, $2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ are coplanar.
questions.solution:
Coplanar means the scalar triple product is $0$:

$\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\2&\lambda&3\\1&2&3\end{vmatrix}=(3\lambda-6)-(6-3)+(4-\lambda)=2\lambda-5=0$, so $\lambda=\dfrac52$.

questions.q: Find the distance of the point $(1,2,3)$ from the plane $2x-y+2z+3=0$.
Find, in degrees, the angle between the planes $x+y=4$ and $x+z=7$.
Find the shortest distance between the skew lines $\vec r=(6\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k)+t(\hat i-2\hat j+2\hat k)$ and $\vec r=(-4\hat i-\hat k)+s(3\hat i-2\hat j-2\hat k)$.
Find the vector and Cartesian equations of the plane passing through the points $(1,2,3)$, $(2,3,1)$ and $(3,1,2)$.
questions.solution:
Let $A(1,2,3)$, $B(2,3,1)$, $C(3,1,2)$. Then $\vec{AB}=(1,1,-2)$ and $\vec{AC}=(2,-1,-1)$.

Normal $\vec n=\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&1&-2\\2&-1&-1\end{vmatrix}=-3\hat i-3\hat j-3\hat k$, parallel to $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$.

**Vector form:** $\vec r\cdot(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)\cdot(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)=6$.

**Cartesian form:** $x+y+z=6$.

Check: $2+3+1=6$ and $3+1+2=6$.
